post.description: Persist a Planning job and return its operation ID. Planning execution and commands follow in BS-018.T2. The same key and typed request return the same operation; a different actor or request conflicts. No publication or execution is implied.

post.description: Record a cancellation request and report what it achieved. Idempotent and monotonic: the first requester and reason are kept. A request after send authorization cannot stop the commit; a terminal job is reported, not changed. Authorization, the cancellation, and its audit record commit together.

503.description: Transient failure; retry the same request

200.description: Cancellation outcome and the job after the request

post.description: Create a fresh-plan retry of a terminal job that did not succeed. The new job links to its source and starts in Planning; no plan, output, or accepted result is reused. The same key and source return the same operation.

503.description: Transient failure; retry the same request

409.description: The source job is not terminal or already succeeded

202.description: Fresh job durably accepted; replay returns the original operation

get.description: Server-sent events for one job, oldest first. Each event's `id` is the job's per-job sequence (1, 2, 3, ...), its `event` is the kind, and its `data` is a JobEvent. Resume with the `Last-Event-ID` header (sent automatically by a reconnecting EventSource) or the `after` query parameter; the header wins. Authorization matches getJob, so unknown and inaccessible jobs are both 404. The stream sends a keep-alive comment every 15 seconds and ends after the event that reaches a terminal state, when the session ends or the caller loses access (checked every 30 seconds without extending the session), or after one hour; reconnect with the last ID seen. A resume point past the job's last event waits for later events, or ends immediately once the job is terminal.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Resume after this sequence; 0 or absent means the start.

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID
parameters.description: The last event ID received; takes precedence over `after`.

200.description: Event stream; each `data` line is a JobEvent

400.description: Invalid resume point or query parameter

503.description: Ledger unavailable or stream capacity exhausted; retry the same request

post.description: Assess a canonical table without creating a job, plan, or output. Reports the baseline, refusals, bins, and estimate. Requires jobs:submit on the table and uses only a catalog connection that grant covers. Bins are capped per response (see bins_total and bins_truncated). No catalog or storage I/O happens until authorization succeeds.

JobEvent.description: The data of one job event. `reason` is set only for transitions, as the typed state reason; operator cancellation text is never included.

snapshot_id.description: 64-bit snapshot ID as a decimal string, so clients that parse JSON numbers as doubles do not round it.
